author: opus 5.5
body: [opus 5.5] Closed: delivered end to end once the provider pushes the thread, with the page as the fallback when it does not. Done in vibe-talk, in the commits 'vibe-talk: put a reply the stream sent without its thread into that thread, and out of Main', 'vibe-talk: tell adapter authors to push message.thread, and test that the page receives it', 'vibe-talk: wait for a read the page gave up on before placing what the stream left unplaced', 'vibe-talk: order All's newest pages by when they were sent, and place what an unfolded one carries', 'vibe-talk: take only the thread record from a replayed copy that places a message', 'vibe-talk: let a newest page of All take out only what the store held when it was sent', 'vibe-talk: keep a reply removed upstream out of the store when the placing read lands' and 'vibe-talk: fold a placing read of All only over the store's copies as they were when it was sent'. The provider half, maintained outside this repository, is reported deployed: the adapter that pushes this channel's live messages now sends each with the thread record its own reads carry, so a threaded reply arrives in its thread and is never drawn on Main. The README push contract documents message.thread, and an ingest test pins that it reaches the page unchanged. The page half covers a live message pushed without a thread record. Once the channel's reads go quiet, the page reads All (reason=place, as a delta where it can) for every such message those reads did not place. Any later copy that names the thread (that read, a delta, a page of any view, a replayed, edited or second live copy) moves the message out of Main into its thread in every column, with its counts, cards and the picker, and the reader keeps their place (#280 scroll-stability). A placing read that fails is asked again when the next read ends. An answer of All the page does not fold still places what it carries, so a bridge that edits its answer while the read is out no longer keeps the reply on Main. Which of two newest pages of All is the newer is decided by the order they were sent in. A placing read is folded only over the store's copies as they were when it was sent, so it takes out no message the store gained since (one the stream delivered, the reader's own send, one another read brought) and undoes no edit Main's read brought while it was out. The read of All for Main's counts speaks only for the messages the store held when it was sent. A message removed upstream, by the stream or a delta's deletions, is no longer left unplaced, so no answer sent before the removal places it or puts it back, and a placing delta out as the stream removed a message is not folded. A replayed copy that places a message gives the store only its thread record. The placing read is never sent beside a read of the channel the page gave up on that the server may still be answering (remote-ops-audit W7); it goes once that read's late answer has landed or failed, and a placing read given up on is kept the same way. Not covered, and older than this series: a column's own newest page that lands late can still hide a message the store gained until the read after it lands (#310 stale-live-read-flicker). The read of All for Main's counts, sent before an edit or a removal and landing after Main's read has brought it, can still undo the edit or bring the removed message back until the next read of All or of the message's thread; that is the same hazard as #310, for a read the page before this series made too. Unverified here: the behaviour against the real provider with the adapter half deployed. A live threaded reply seen arriving straight in its thread, and one pushed without its record leaving Main once the placing read lands, is the owner's check. Everything above was shown by the page suite and the ingest test, not on a deployment.
